Things I wish I knew BEFORE visiting Marrakech, Morocco 🇲🇦👇🏼 If you’re planning a trip to Marrakech for the first time, SAVE this because these Marrakech travel tips would have made our trip so much easier! From getting around Marrakech to booking attractions, exploring the souks and even travelling with a drone, here are a few things to know before visiting Marrakech 👇🏼 📍 Getting around Marrakech — we found the inDrive app much easier because you can see the price before accepting the ride rather than negotiating with taxis. 🌿 Jardin Majorelle tickets — BOOK IN ADVANCE! This is one of the most popular things to do in Marrakech and tickets can sell out. 🕌 Madrasa Ben Youssef — we bought our tickets when we arrived, so you don’t necessarily need to pre-book this one. 🚁 Bringing a drone to Morocco — drones are restricted in Morocco. As full-time travellers carrying ours onwards, we declared it on arrival and left it with customs to collect again when leaving. 🛍️ Marrakech souks — bargaining is normal, so look around and compare prices before buying. SAVE the shops you like on Google Maps too because finding the same stall again in the Marrakech Medina is harder than you think 😂 If you’re searching for a Marrakech travel guide, Marrakech itinerary, where to stay in Marrakech, Marrakech food recommendations or the best things to do in Marrakech, I have a whole Morocco travel series on my page 🇲🇦 Next stop… South of France 🇫🇷👀 Follow for realistic travel guides, itineraries and tips from our full-time travels! #marrakesh #morocco #travelguide #traveltipsgreece  #creatorsearchinsights

Four days in Marrakech, Morocco and I already can't wait to go back! 🇲🇦✨ If you’re planning your first trip to Morocco, Marrakech is the perfect place to dive into the country’s rich culture, incredible food, and beautiful architecture. Between getting lost in the medina, learning to cook traditional Moroccan dishes, and enjoying a little luxury in the Agafay Desert, we packed SO much into four days! One thing I loved most about Marrakech was how every day felt completely different. You can spend one morning exploring centuries of history and the next relaxing poolside with views of the Atlas Mountains. And the hospitality? Some of the best I’ve experienced. 🥹 My biggest recommendation is to leave some room in your Marrakech itinerary to wander, shop, and enjoy the city without rushing from one attraction to the next. 📌 Save this 4-day Marrakech itinerary for your Morocco vacation, and tell me: Would you rather spend a day exploring the souks or relaxing in the Agafay Desert? #MarrakechMorocco #MarrakechItinerary #MoroccoTravel #VisitMarrakech #blacktravelblogger things to do in Marrakech, Marrakech itinerary

5 things to know before going to Morocco👇🇲🇦 1️⃣ Always carry cash. Morocco is still very cash-based, especially in local shops, markets and smaller restaurants. 💵 2️⃣ Be a responsible tourist. Think twice before paying for animal encounters in Marrakech, particularly the monkeys and snakes in Jemaa el-Fnaa. 🐒 3️⃣ Explore beyond Marrakech. Some of Morocco’s best experiences are outside the city, so make time for places like Chefchaouen, Volubilis and the Atlas Mountains. 🏜️ 4️⃣ Having mobile data when you land makes your arrival so much easier. It’s my last morning in Morocco, and I’m sitting in the back of the car on the way to the airport trying to wrap my head around how much we squeezed into two weeks. I landed in Casablanca on my own, and somewhere between Rabat, the Roman ruins at Volubilis, and getting henna in Fez, I was already thinking about how much I was going to miss this trip. Fez alone could’ve filled my entire camera roll. The alleyways in the medina, the markets, the cats I obviously had to stop and film, and the rug shop where I somehow decided four rugs and an ottoman was a perfectly reasonable outcome. 😂 Then came the Sahara, Ouarzazate, Aït Ben Haddou, and finally Marrakesh. I’m still laughing that out of everything I filmed in Morocco, the dog riding on a scooter was the one so many of you loved as much as I did. One of my favorite things about showing up solo is that you have no idea who you’ll end up sharing the trip with. I got really lucky with this group. Even when our van battery died and we had to pile into taxis, everybody just rolled with it. I’ll miss sitting down to dinner together and laughing about whatever happened that day. And I’m so grateful to the people who took the time to share their traditions with me, show me how things were made, and answer my million questions. That’s the part I’ll still be talking about when someone asks me how Morocco was six months from now. And to everyone who followed along, especially the Moroccans who popped into my comments to tell me more about the places I was visiting or explain something I’d just seen for the first time, thank you. It was so fun getting to share this trip with people who love Morocco and call it home. I’d do it all again. I’d probably just buy the extra suitcase a little earlier next time. 😂 Thank you for the best two weeks, Morocco. I’m really going to miss you. 🇲🇦❤️#passporttherapy #travel #traveltok #morocco #moroccanmemories
